newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Tamil rebels ready for clash with Sri Lanka army.
newsitem.headline: Tamil rebels ready for clash with Sri Lanka army.

text.p: Sri Lanka's Tamil Tiger rebels said on Thursday that large numbers of guerrillas were ready for a "tremendous clash" with government troops advancing into the rebel-held northwestern region.
"(Our) fighters are strategically placed to meet the oncoming Sinhala (Sri Lankan) army in what will be a tremendous clash," the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) said in a statement.
The Defence Ministry has declined to reveal the aim of the military's latest offensive which was launched on February 4 from Vavuniya, a government stronghold 220 km (138 miles) northeast of Colombo.
By Thursday, the army had spent a week building fortifications along their 22-km (14 mile) thrust into rebel-held territory, a Defence Ministry spokesman said.
Commenting on the latest LTTE statement, the spokesman said the army was expecting resistance when they advance deeper into rebel areas.
"It is a vast area, mostly jungle," the ministry spokesman said. "Also, our advance is slowed by the need to clear mines and boobytraps."
Rebel resistance so far has been light and the army has had no casualties in the offensive, the largest this year.

The LTTE claimed the army planned to open a route from Colombo all the way to Jaffna peninsula on the northern tip of the Indian Ocean island. It said the military would be vulnerable in such a thrust.
"This will leave the stretched-out army extremely vulnerable while highly-motivated LTTE fighters are poised in massive numbers ready to attack," the LTTE said.
The LTTE also accused the military of burning crops planted by Tamil villagers and of bombing and bulldozing their homes.
Statements by the LTTE are not rare but comments on a specific army offensive are unusual.
The Defence Ministry spokesman denied the accusations.
The LTTE radio station, monitored by Reuters on Thursday, said the rebels lost 14 fighters, including 10 officers, at sea in fighting off Iranaitivu island, north of Mannar, last Saturday.

It was not clear if the LTTE radio was referring to a defence ministry report which said navy patrols blew up a large LTTE boat returning from south India, where the rebels are known to keep safe houses.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the rebels' 14-year war for independence for minority Tamils in the north and east but the LTTE says the toll is much higher.
